title: introduce-stream-hook-adapter-rotate-auth-window-typed-cursors
author: Evelyn Huang
release_notes: Adds a StreamHookAdapter to unify stream lifecycle hooks across SDKs, rotates short-lived token window to reduce reauth jitter, introduces typed Cursor/Iterator helpers for ergonomic consumption, and bumps SDK package versions.
description:
Motivation: SDK consumers reported inconsistent stream lifecycle hooks (onOpen/onChunk/onClose) and reauth behavior across Python/TS/Go. This caused subtle bugs when applications relied on deterministic reconnect semantics and led to duplicate reauth attempts under load. This PR unifies the consumer surface and reduces auth jitter by moving to a rotating short-lived token window with centralized jitter logic.

What I changed (single PR touching all three SDKs):
- Introduced StreamHookAdapter (Python: StreamHookAdapter, TS: StreamHookAdapter, Go: streamhook.Adapter) that normalizes onOpen/onData/onEnd/onError semantics and provides an optional rewindable Cursor helper.
- Added typed Cursor/Iterator helpers to expose a consistent, lazy iterator API for streaming consumers.
- Implemented rotating auth-window in client core: refreshes credentials earlier with randomized jitter slot to avoid stampeding reauths.
- Parity fixes: aligned error codes and retry decisions across SDKs; consolidated backoff defaults to 200ms base/ multiplier 1.5/ cap 10s.
- Ergonomics: renamed 'resume_stream' -> 'resume' on client instances and added deprecation warnings for old method.
- Tests: unit tests for each SDK, cross-SDK e2e smoke for stream resumption, flakey incident test added and stabilized.
- Docs: updated quickstarts and migration notes; added code examples for the Cursor helpers.
- Version bumps: python 0.12.4, typescript 1.8.0, go 0.9.3.

Backward compatibility & migration notes:
- 'resume_stream' alias remains for one release with deprecation warnings; users should switch to 'resume' method.
- StreamHookAdapter is opt-in: existing consumers continue to receive previous callbacks unless they opt into the adapter.

Why this approach: Centralizing lifecycle hooks reduces duplicated logic in clients and makes cross-language behavior predictable for platform teams. Rotating auth window prevents thundering reauth storms observed during high-throughput canaries. The Cursor helpers aim to reduce boilerplate for consumer code that previously had to manage buffer/kv cache interactions directly.
